title: Kubelet OOMScore adaptive eviction experiment notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working note capturing an exploratory experiment to reduce noisy/cascading evictions during transient node memory pressure by using adaptive oom_score_adj hints and softer eviction thresholds for cache-heavy inference pods. The goal is to give long-lived worker processes a better chance to shed caches or restart gracefully without triggering top-of-stack scheduler thrashing.

Context / motivation:
- Production: Dedicated GPU nodes running multiple inference workers showed spikes of simultaneous pod evictions when ephemeral memory pressure hit p95-p99.
- Observed symptom: rapid series of kubelet evictions (memory.available) followed by scheduler reshuffle and high API-server churn. Pod restarts sometimes triggered OOMKill loops on the same host due to aggressive oom_score ordering.
- Hypothesis: default oom_score behavior + static eviction thresholds cause a noisy cascade; prioritizing which processes the OOM killer prefers and allowing kubelet to delay eviction for cacheable processes might reduce churn and improve tail latency for serving.

Timeline (experiment run):
- 2025-11-05: initial notes and design sketch (this doc created).
- 2025-11-18: small-scale A/B on staging GPU pool (n1-standard + 1 A100).
- 2025-12-02: adjust kubelet flag set and containerRuntimeConfig to expose oom_score_adj annotations.
- 2025-12-09: observed fewer simultaneous evictions, but two pods hit OOMKill after delayed eviction window.
- 2026-01-30: rolled improved heuristics to canary 10% of Dedicated nodes.

Key observations (metrics / logs):
- PromQL used:
  - rate(kubelet_eviction_total[5m]) by (node) shows a ~32% reduction on canary nodes during synthetic pressure tests.
  - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes drop patterns unchanged, but pod eviction count decoupled from peak memory dips by ~8s median.
- dmesg snippets on affected hosts show kernel oom_reaper ordering matching oom_score_adj hints we set.
- kubelet logs included: "eviction manager: attempt to reclaim memory, soft eviction of resource memory.available" followed by either kubelet kill or kubelet eviction (depending on timing).

Experiment design (what we changed):
1) Expose a new pod annotation: "oom.adaptive.redwood.io/score-hint" with values "prefer-keep", "neutral", "prefer-kill".
   - Implemented via containerRuntimeConfig hook that sets /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj for the main pid of the container when the runtime launches the process.
2) Kubelet config change (canary only): add an eviction soft threshold for memory.available at 3% (softGracePeriod 15s) rather than immediate hard eviction at 2%.
3) A helper sidecar (optional) added for cache-heavy processes to watch RSS vs cache and proactively drop caches on SIGUSR1.
4) Monitoring: add Grafana panel tracking per-node "eviction-delay" metric (time between soft threshold trigger and actual eviction) and per-pod OOMKill counts.

Playbook (on-call quick steps during a pressure event while canary is active):
- Triage: check Grafana cluster/evictions dashboard -> identify if canary nodes are active
- If evictions spike and OOMKills climb:
  1) ssh to node (if necessary) and run: free -h; ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 10; cat /proc/*/oom_score_adj | sed -n '1,40p' to spot mismatches.
  2) kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep Evicted -m 50
  3) If many pods with "prefer-keep" hint are getting OOMKilled, temporarily set kubelet eviction softGracePeriod to 0 to force immediate eviction to protect node stability (kubectl patch cm kubelet-config -n kube-system --type merge -p '{"data":{"evictionHard":"memory.available<1%"}}') and restart kubelet in rolling fashion.
- Rollback: revert the oom_score_adj injection by scaling daemonset that performs the adjustment to 0, or remove the containerRuntimeConfig entry.

Reproduction recipe (staging):
- Spin up 3-node staging GPU pool with same machine type as prod (g4dn-...) and deploy the inference worker with: 
  - annotation: oom.adaptive.redwood.io/score-hint=prefer-keep
  - sidecar that calls 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' on SIGUSR1
- Run memory pressure generator on other pods to produce short bursts: stress-ng --vm 2 --vm-bytes 80% --timeout 60s repeated with jitter.
- Observe kubelet eviction timeline and kernel oom logs.

Risks and failure modes noted:
- If the kernel ignores oom_score_adj ordering under extreme memory fragmentation, we may delay evictions but still trigger kernel OOMKill of arbitrary processes (worse outcome).
- Introducing a delay window increases chance of node swap (if enabled) or general instability; we prefer to keep swap off.
- Sidecar-based drop_caches may mask memory pressure symptoms and produce misleading metrics for long-term capacity planning.

Follow-ups / next steps (action items):
- (Aisha) Implement more robust runtime hook that sets oom_score_adj only for main container PID and reports the applied value to node exporter (due 2026-02-01).
- (Liam) Add canary automation that will revert setting automatically if OOMKill rate > 0.5/min over 5m window (due 2026-01-20).
- (Claire) Run a 24h soak test under representative traffic and record p99 latency, eviction count, and OOMKill events (due 2026-01-10).
- Product/alerts: create PagerDuty policy to only page SRE on sustained >5/min evictions across >2 nodes to reduce noise.

Open questions (to be decided):
- Do we prefer kernel-level control (oom_score_adj) or letting kubelet make smarter pod selection based on QoS class and usage patterns?
- Should we bake the hint annotation into our operator for inference workloads only, or make it a general platform feature?
- How do we reconcile long-lived caches and tenant isolation in Dedicated pools (risk of noisy-neighbor cache hogs)?

Notes to self / drafts: 
- Consider integrating with cgroup v2 OOM control knobs (memory.pressure persistency) once node kernels are standardized across regions.
- Look into whether cri-o/containerd already provide lifecycle hooks we can reuse instead of a full daemonset.

References and links:
- Linear: RED-234 (tracking implementation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-tools/pull/412 (oomscore injection prototype)
- Grafana: cluster/evictions dashboard panel id (linked above)
- Kernel docs: Documentation/filesystems/proc.txt (oom_score_adj behavior)
